papers.title: A Gaussian Process State Space Formulation for Materials Constitutive Modeling: Application to Quasi-brittle Materials
papers.abstract: Constitutive models for history-dependent, path-dependent materials typically encode this dependence in prescribed functional forms through internal variables such as damage or plastic strain that are phenomenological, model-dependent, and not directly observable. These rigid forms lack flexibility to match observations, make calibration potentially non-unique, and complicate uncertainty quantification. This paper develops a Gaussian-process state-space model (GP-SSM) that replaces the fixed form of the constitutive model with a flexible GP regression, and the prescribed internal variables with latent state variables learned directly from observable stress-strain histories. As a GP, the model is naturally endowed with a measure of uncertainty and can be constrained to satisfy physical principles. We demonstrate this framework for quasi-brittle materials under triaxial compression, where the latent variable evolution is driven by the current-state stress invariants and the increment of equivalent strain to reflect irreversible, pressure-sensitive history. A sparse multi-output GP then maps the latent state and current strain tensor to the six-component stress response, trained by variational sparse inference. The trained model is exported into Abaqus/Explicit through a user material subroutine. Four verification cases are reported: (1) offline rollout on validation and test histories; (2) a single element under changing confinement; (3) a frozen-memory unloading-reloading extension; and (4) a multi-element structural model compared against the Karagozian and Case Concrete (KCC) model. These results show that the learned state-space update reproduces held-out RVE-scale histories in closed-loop rollout, tracks evolving confinement, supports unloading without violating the irreversibility of the learned history state, and reproduces structural-level behavior consistent with KCC.

papers.title: Multi-Fidelity Particle Flow Filters based on Log Homotopy
papers.abstract: This work proposes a new Multi-Fidelity Particle Flow Filter (MFPFF) based on a linear control variate framework and multilevel Monte Carlo methods. Conventional particle filters often suffer from weight collapse and particle degeneracy in high-dimensional spaces. Particle flow filters address this by smoothly transporting prior particles toward the posterior distribution, thereby avoiding the need for resampling. This work constructs multi-fidelity particle flow filters by augmenting a small number of expensive high-fidelity particles (full-order model runs) with a large number of inexpensive low-resolution particles (reduced-order surrogates constructed via intrusive Galerkin projection). These surrogates act as control variates to enhance the statistical estimate of the full-order posterior, yielding enhanced analysis accuracy at comparable computational cost. The work focuses on two particle flows based on log homotopy, the stochastic Gromov flow and deterministic Exact flow. Numerical experiments with the Korteweg-De Vries (KdV) and Quasi-Geostrophic (QG) test problems demonstrate that the proposed MFPFF achieves accuracy comparable to high-fidelity simulations while significantly reducing computational expense.

papers.title: ADACT: PDE-Constrained Thermal Hardware/Software Co-Design Adjoint-Driven Optimal Control via Finite Difference Discretization
papers.abstract: By virtue of the sheer compute demands of large-scale artificial intelligence (AI) and high-performance computing (HPC), modern multi-core microprocessors suffer from severe power density limits and thermal throttling, entailing an urgent need for principled methods for predictive, physics-informed dynamical thermal management (DTM). Here, we introduce a hardware/software co-design physics-informed PDE-constrained DTM throttling optimal control algorithm, ADACT (Adjoint-Driven Adaptive Co-Design Thermal Control), that minimizes thermal risk and cooling energy overhead while maximizing core execution throughput. The underlying physical temperature field is governed by a two-dimensional nonhomogeneous parabolic reaction-diffusion equation with spatially localized, time-varying power source terms and variable convective cooling subject to nonhomogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. We employ a discretization of the continuous state PDE via a Crank-Nicolson finite difference scheme with a 5-point discrete Laplacian operator on a uniform spatial mesh, which preserves unconditional numerical stability and $O(\Delta x^2 + \Delta y^2 + \Delta t^2)$ second-order temporal and spatial accuracy. To efficiently compute exact gradients, we construct and implement a continuous backward-in-time adjoint state method with L-BFGS as our optimization algorithm of choice. The accuracy and second-order convergence rates of both forward state and backward adjoint solvers are quantitatively verified via the Method of Manufactured Solutions (MMS), and gradient accuracy is validated using directional derivative Taylor tests. Numerical experiments demonstrate that ADACT dynamically throttles software power workloads and modulates hardware cooling efforts to strictly uphold physical thermal thresholds while maintaining operational throughput.

papers.title: Derivative-Informed Dimension Reduction of Stochastic Differential Equations: A Path-Space Sensitivity Approach
papers.abstract: Uncertainty in the drift of a stochastic differential equation (SDE) induces uncertainty in statistical observables defined as expected functionals on path space. We propose a derivative-informed method for identifying low-dimensional structure in the drift-to-observable map, with the aim of improving the tractability of uncertainty quantification. This approach can be viewed as a generalization of the active subspace method to infinite-dimensional input spaces and to path-space observables of SDEs. Representing uncertainty in the drift by random perturbations in a Hilbert space, we construct a path-space sensitivity operator using first-order Fr\'echet derivatives of the observable with respect to the perturbation. We establish conditions under which the leading eigenfunctions of this operator correspond to directions of maximum mean squared sensitivity of the observable, thus enabling low-dimensional approximation with certified error bounds. We further introduce a martingale control variate of the Fr\'echet derivative that reduces error in sample-based estimators of the operator. Using a Galerkin scheme for numerical discretization, we show that reduced representations of the drift from the derivative-informed basis yield more accurate approximations of mean first hitting times of SDEs than the Karhunen-Lo\`eve expansion of the same truncation order.

papers.title: Hybridizable Discontinuous Galerkin methods for the Keller-Segel model
papers.abstract: We propose a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) finite element method to approximate the solution of the time-dependent Keller-Segel model, a drift-diffusion system describing chemotactic cell movement. We develop and analyze the corresponding HDG scheme, and establish theoretical convergence results for the proposed discretization. Finally, we present numerical experiments that confirm the theoretical findings.

papers.title: Robust augmented Block Preconditioning for two-phase Incompressible Inductionless MHD
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a robust augmented block preconditioner for three-dimensional, two-phase, incompressible inductionless MHD equations. We employ a high-order monolithic and charge-conservative arbitrary Lagrangian--Eulerian (ALE) finite element method as base scheme, for which the solution variables are current density, velocity, electric potential and pressure. Grad-div stabilization is added in both the current density equation and discrete momentum equation. Backward Euler method is used for the time discretization. At each time step, fully coupled solution strategy is adopted. This leads to large-scale, ill-conditioned, nonsymmetric, and indefinite dual saddle-point system. To solve this system efficiently, we construct an augmented block preconditioner within the constraint preconditioning framework. The ultimate preconditioner combines the augmented Lagrangian technique with approximate block factorization for current density sub-system and fluid sub-system. The fully coupled four-field system is then solved using preconditioned FGMRES iteration. Numerical experiments confirm the high-order accuracy and discrete charge conservation of the ALE-FEM. Drop of heavy fluid in light fluid is taken as benchmark to demonstrate the robustness of the preconditioner with respect to the discontinuity of physical parameters and the mesh size.

papers.title: Optimization-based Cell Average Limiters as Metric Projections: Constrained Evolution and Convergence Analysis for Convection-diffusion Equations
papers.abstract: The optimization-based cell average limiter enforces global conservation and bounds, and has been successfully applied to discontinuous Galerkin (DG) discretizations of a wide range of nonlinear systems, from phase-field models to the compressible Navier-Stokes equations. In this paper, taking the heat and convection-diffusion equations as prototypes, we analyze the convergence of the scheme resulting from cell average limiting. Encoding conservation and admissibility in a differential inclusion identifies the limiter as a backward Euler proximal step in a Lie splitting of the constrained evolution. This proximal step is the metric projection onto the convex admissible set, and we prove that it is nonexpansive and stable in the $L^2$ norm, and that it does not increase the total variation of the cell averages. Combined with the standard error analysis, nonexpansiveness yields an $O(\tau+h^{k+1})$ estimate for implicit Euler time stepping with DG discretization of polynomial degree $k$ under a reverse CFL condition, together with an unconditional $O(\tau+h^{k})$ estimate. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted convergence rates and the enforcement of the bounds.

papers.title: An improved fast iterative moment method for the simulation of near-continuum gas flows with Shakhov model
papers.abstract: The fast iterative moment (FIM) method developed in [G. Li, C. Wang, and Z. Hu, Comput. Fluids, 311 (2026), 107031] achieves fast convergence for near-continuum gas flows modeled by the Boltzmann-BGK equation through alternating iterations between the high-order moment system and the consistent hydrodynamic equations. In this paper, we extend the FIM solver to the Shakhov model and improve it in the following aspects. A finite volume method with linear reconstruction is employed for high-resolution spatial discretization of both systems. Following the original FIM method, an implicit-explicit scheme treating the Shakhov collision term implicitly is adopted for the high-order moment system. A local Fourier analysis of a linearized one-dimensional BGK model reveals the need for more hydrodynamic iterations at smaller Knudsen numbers and their slower convergence on refined grids. Motivated by these findings, a Newton-multigrid method with a new regularization strategy is introduced for the hydrodynamic equations, generally providing an effective hydrodynamic correction with one step per alternating iteration, thereby reducing the need for empirical tuning. Numerical experiments for planar Couette flow, lid-driven cavity flow, and heat transfer in a bottom-heated cavity are carried out to investigate the performance of the improved FIM solver. The results demonstrate improved efficiency and robustness over the original FIM method, particularly at small Knudsen numbers, and favorable performance with both first- and second-order spatial discretizations.

papers.title: Inverse problems with fractional operators: an analytical study and its numerical linear algebra treatment via the GLT theory
papers.abstract: Fractional derivatives model memory effects and nonlocal interactions beyond classical integer-order models. Fractional differential equations (FDEs) thus describe anomalous diffusion, transport in heterogeneous media, and hereditary dynamics. Their nonlocality, however, makes inverse problems challenging: unknown sources, coefficients, or initial conditions must be recovered from indirect and noisy data. Inverse problems for FDEs are usually ill-posed in the Hadamard sense, so regularization, such as the quasi-boundary value method, is required for stable reconstruction. Discretization produces large linear systems whose matrices inherit the nonlocal structure of fractional operators. Understanding the asymptotic spectral properties of these matrix sequences is essential for efficient solvers and preconditioners. Generalized Locally Toeplitz (GLT) theory provides a unified framework for the spectral distribution of large structured matrices and for preconditioner design. This thesis uses GLT theory to analyze matrix sequences from inverse problems for FDEs, construct structure-preserving preconditioners, and study nonlinear operations in the GLT algebra. In particular, it proves maximal distribution results for geometric means of GLT sequences: when the symbols commute, the geometric mean sequence remains GLT without symbol invertibility. This resolves a long-standing conjecture and shows maximality in the noncommuting degenerate case. Overall, the thesis integrates regularization, spectral analysis, and preconditioning into a coherent computational framework for inverse problems in nonlocal fractional dynamics, while enriching structured matrix analysis.

papers.title: On the stability of second-order methods for DDEs and PDDEs
papers.abstract: In this paper, a one-parameter family of second-order implicit--explicit (IMEX) multistep methods is studied for delay differential equations (DDEs). The analysis is based on the matrix problem $y'(t)=A y(t) + B y(t-\tau(t))$, where $A$ is Hermitian negative definite but $B$ is any matrix. For constant, grid-aligned delays, a field-of-values argument yields unconditional stability whenever a suitable generalized field of values $F_p(A,B)$ is contained in the open unit disk. For a constant non-grid-aligned delay, we show that quadratic interpolation does not reduce the corresponding stability disk. For genuinely variable delays, the method is formulated as a nonautonomous augmented system, and product-level sufficient conditions are obtained from a common quadratic Lyapunov inequality and from a quantitative slow-variation hypothesis. The approach developed herein is illustrated through several examples in which the discussed theory is applied not only to DDEs, but also to semidiscrete parabolic problems given by partial delay differential equations with a diffusion term.

papers.title: The Exact Dihedral Angle Sum Range for Circumcentral-Cevian Jaw Tetrahedra
papers.abstract: Hajja, Hammoudeh, Hayajneh and Martini showed that a tetrahedron whose cevians to the circumcenters of the opposite faces are concurrent is either a kite or a special jaw. We determine the exact dihedral-angle-sum range on the jaw component. The lower endpoint is attained only by the regular tetrahedron, while the upper endpoint is approached only in the degenerate limit. The proof reduces the family to one scale-invariant parameter and an explicit monotonicity argument.

papers.title: Greedy Orthogonal Polynomial Manifolds with Lipschitz Control for Dimensionality Reduction and Reduced Modeling
papers.abstract: Polynomial manifolds provide nonlinear low-dimensional representations through polynomial decoders. We propose to represent the polynomial terms of the decoder using features that are orthonormal on the training data. This empirical orthogonality enables a greedy algorithm, Greedy-OPM, which jointly selects encoder modes and polynomial features while minimizing the reconstruction error under a prescribed bound on the decoder's Lipschitz constant. Numerical experiments show that this Lipschitz constraint improves generalization away from the training data while retaining high reconstruction accuracy.

papers.title: An optimization-based property-preserving limiter for two-phase flow in porous media on non-matching meshes
papers.abstract: Two-phase flow in porous media arises in a wide range of applications in engineering and science. A fundamental challenge in its numerical simulation is that the approximation of the saturation transport equation can violate the maximum principle, and spurious oscillations can appear even when the solution remains within physical bounds. In this work, we propose a bound-preserving anti-oscillation postprocessing limiter for discontinuous Galerkin discretizations of the two-phase flow system on non-matching meshes. An optimization-based cell average limiter enforces the prescribed bounds on the cell averages while preserving global mass by minimizing the $L^2$ distance to the original cell averages. To suppress the remaining oscillations, the cell average limiter is combined with a minmod limiter, which is activated only in the cells identified by a troubled-cell detector to avoid unnecessary loss of accuracy, and a Zhang-Shu scaling limiter subsequently enforces the bounds on point values. In addition, we prove that the cell average limiter preserves the accuracy of the numerical solution at a fixed time on non-matching meshes. Numerical experiments on homogeneous, non-homogeneous, and fractured porous media demonstrate the accuracy and robustness of the proposed method.

papers.title: The Calder\'on problem for the multi-fractional Laplacian Schr\"{o}dinger equation with drift terms
papers.abstract: This paper studies the Calder\'on inverse problem for the multi-fractional Laplacian Schr\"odinger equation with drift terms, whose leading operator is a sum of fractional Laplacians of different orders, perturbed by a drift vector field and a potential. We consider two inverse settings: in the homogeneous source case \(f=0\), we aim to simultaneously recover the drift coefficient \(b\) and the potential \(q\) from the associated Dirichlet-to-Neumann map; in the non-homogeneous case \(f\neq 0\), we aim to simultaneously determine \(b\), \(q\), and the source term \(f\). Under suitable assumptions, we establish the well-posedness of the forward problem, derive a strong unique continuation principle, prove Runge-type approximation properties in fractional Sobolev spaces and weighted \(C^k\) spaces, and obtain generalized Alessandrini identities. These tools yield global uniqueness results for the inverse problems. In addition, we develop a numerical reconstruction framework combining finite difference discretization, radial basis function surrogate modeling, and hierarchical Bayesian inversion. Numerical examples in one dimension for smooth and discontinuous coefficients and sources illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method and support the theoretical uniqueness results.

papers.title: Convergence Analysis of Variable-Separation-Based Model Reduction for Linear Parametric Partial Differential Equations
papers.abstract: This paper analyzes the convergence of a variable-separation (VS) model reduction method that successively constructs separated approximations to the solutions of linear parametric partial differential equations (PDEs) by solving residual problems at sampled parameter values. We prove that the resulting VS approximations converge almost surely to the exact parametric solution in the parameter-averaged energy norm, under finite-dimensional approximation conditions on the error family and the assumptions of symmetry, uniform coercivity, and uniform boundedness of the governing bilinear forms. For parametric PDEs whose operators and right-hand sides admit finite-term separated representations, we construct finite-dimensional approximation spaces for the error family and bound their dimensions and approximation errors, thereby verifying these approximation conditions and obtaining an $O((\log N)^{-1})$ upper bound for the expected parameter-averaged error energy after $N$ iterations. When the solution families are contained in a fixed finite-dimensional space, we obtain the sharper $O(N^{-1})$ bound for the expected error energy and, if the operator is also parameter-independent, exact recovery for almost every parameter after an almost surely finite number of iterations. Numerical experiments illustrate the error decay of the VS approximations, as well as finite-step recovery in the parameter-independent case.

papers.title: An efficient method for reconstructing the potential in the fractional Calder\'on problem with a single measurement
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a numerical method for determining the potential function in one-dimensional and two-dimensional fractional-order Calder\'{o}n problems through a single measurement. The fractional Laplacian is discretized using the finite difference method, and the POD-RBF method is used to construct the forward problem surrogate model that can provide the predicted value and its exact gradient in time. The inverse problem is solved using Tikhonov regularization and the conjugate gradient method. The efficiency and effectiveness of the developed method are demonstrated through numerical experiments, and the theoretical results are verified.

papers.title: Numerical Construction of Quasi-Periodic Solutions for Nonlinear PDEs: II. Unbounded Perturbation
papers.abstract: Many nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) arising in physical models involve unbounded perturbations, where nonlinear terms contain spatial derivatives. Such perturbations can be expressed as compositions of unbounded operators with bounded nonlinear maps. In this paper, we propose alternating numerical schemes for constructing quasi-periodic solutions to this class of PDEs, including the nonlinear acoustic wave (NLAW) equation and the Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation. To render the nonlinear perturbations bounded, we apply inverse differential operators as a preconditioning; this, however, also rescales the linear part by polynomial factors in the spatial mode $n$. Two main difficulties arise. The first is to control the measure of the resulting ``bad'' frequencies, since the bounds on the measures of the excluded frequency sets are enlarged by polynomial factors in $n$; we show that this measure nevertheless remains small. The second concerns resonances involving the perturbed eigenvalues of the linearized operator at large scales. Our key observation is that, when the dispersive frequencies grow polynomially in $n$ with degree greater than one, such resonances cannot occur if the magnitude of the temporal index lies below a threshold proportional to $|n|$ raised to one less than that degree. It therefore suffices to consider the complementary regime, in which the growth induced by the unbounded perturbation can be controlled in terms of the temporal index. At large scales, an additional complication arises: for a given spatial index $n$, all temporal indices in a box may be ``bad''. We show, however, that at each scale there is at most one such spatial index. Consequently, the resulting counting loss is only polynomial and can be absorbed into the exponential-logarithmic threshold, allowing us once again to retain control over the measures of the excluded frequency sets.

papers.title: ESPC-Transolver: An Equivalent-Surface Physics-Guided Coupling-Aware Transolver for 3D Multiple Scattering
papers.abstract: Cross-geometry generalization is particularly challenging because geometry-conditioned multiple-scattering surrogates must infer unseen objects' scattering properties from geometric features while accurately capturing complex, phase-sensitive interactions arising from repeated wave exchange. We introduce ESPC-Transolver, an equivalent-surface physics-guided, coupling-aware Transolver that separates local scattering-response representations from inter-object interaction modeling. For each sound-hard scatterer, canonical scattered-pressure responses are constructed under a shared set of spherical-wave excitations. A local Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DtN) map and modal scattering conversion express these responses on an enclosing sphere, providing physically consistent input channels across geometries. Shared object-local Transolver blocks encode these responses and incident-field traces, while relative-position-aware slice attention models inter-object coupling. Predicted interface pressure and normal flux recovered from the local operator define equivalent sources for reconstructing exterior near- and far-field scattering. We evaluate the method on three-dimensional acoustic multiple-scattering problems at a fixed frequency, comparing it with geometry-conditioned predictors and alternative neural network backbones. ESPC-Transolver achieves lower scattered-field prediction errors on held-out instances of familiar geometry families and generalizes effectively to previously unseen Peanut and Torus geometries. Exterior-field reconstructions reproduce multiple-scattering interference patterns, linking cross-geometry interface prediction to near-field pressure and far-field scattering recovery.

papers.title: Recovering fractal boundary dimensions from Robin eigenvalues
papers.abstract: We study Robin problems in which a small local boundary coefficient competes with the increasing surface measure of a finite-depth fractal approximation. For a fixed smooth domain, layer potentials give Green function and eigenpair expansions; contour residues and a finite-rank reduction yield a quantitative spectral-gap-dependent eigenvalue remainder. For varying Lipschitz domains, a uniform Poincar\'e inequality and a trace estimate with respect to normalized surface measure give a uniform ground-state expansion and a rank-one resolvent singularity as the total Robin boundary mass tends to zero. Under the boundary-resolution hypothesis and the condition on the approximation scales, ground-state measurements with known Robin coefficients recover the lower and upper Minkowski dimensions for sequences with bounded total Robin boundary mass. We describe Neumann, generalized Robin, and Dirichlet-type operator limits under the corresponding compact Mosco convergence hypotheses. Koch snowflake computations illustrate the reconstruction formulas, and an exact finite-stage area correction improves the adjacent-stage dimension estimator.

papers.title: Lie Symmetry-Guided Adaptive Sampling for Physics-Informed Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have emerged as a promising mesh-free framework for solving partial differential equations (PDEs), with broad applications in physics, engineering, and medicine. However, their performance is highly sensitive to the sampling strategy for training points. Conventional uniform sampling often fails to adequately resolve regions with complex solution features, leading to low efficiency and limited accuracy. To address these challenges, we propose a Lie symmetry-driven adaptive sampling framework for PINNs, termed Lie-AS-ISC. For PDEs admitting Lie symmetry groups, symmetry transformations are exploited to derive intrinsic functional relationships between the solution and its variables, enabling the construction of basis points with exact solutions that span the solution domain. Building on this, an adaptive sampling strategy is developed by jointly considering absolute error and invariant surface conditions, while a dual-index loss is introduced to enhance training constraints. The proposed method significantly improves prediction accuracy. The experimental results show that this method consistently outperforms existing methods in accuracy.

papers.title: Second-Order Steps, Spectral Accuracy: Discrete Parallel Transport of Invariant Subspaces
papers.abstract: Eigensolvers return orthonormal bases of invariant subspaces, but each basis is determined only up to a unitary factor, so bases computed at different parameter values cannot, in general, be interpolated directly. Discrete parallel transport resolves this ambiguity by aligning consecutive bases through the polar factors of their overlaps, but approximates the continuous parallel-transported frame only to second order. We show that the resulting frames can nevertheless be interpolated with spectral accuracy. For analytic families of invariant subspaces sampled at $N+1$ Chebyshev nodes, the computed frames are exact samples of an analytic frame related to the parallel-transported frame by a gauge that remains within $O(N^{-2})$ of the identity throughout a fixed complex neighborhood, uniformly in $N$. Consequently, Chebyshev interpolation approximates this analytic frame with geometric convergence. Moreover, the continuous parallel-transported frame can be recovered to spectral accuracy by solving a small matrix differential equation, without additional eigensolves or derivatives of the underlying matrix family. The results do not require the family to be Hermitian and remain valid through eigenvalue crossings and branch points, provided the selected invariant subspace depends analytically on the parameter. Numerical examples confirm the predicted rates.

papers.title: Energy stability of explicit--implicit--null time discretizations for nonlinear degenerate parabolic equations with state-dependent coefficients
papers.abstract: We study nonlinear degenerate parabolic equations with state-dependent coefficients admitting a scalar energy potential. The explicit--implicit--null (EIN) method avoids severe time step restrictions of explicit time stepping and costly Newton--Raphson iterations required by a fully implicit treatment of the nonlinearity. Using orthogonal projection of the Kirchhoff transform, we prove nonlinear energy stability for first- to third-order EIN time stepping coupled with a wide range of spatial discretizations that admit self-adjoint positive semidefinite discrete operators. Under an upper bound for the diffusion coefficient on relevant stage segments, two IMEX coefficient conditions yield sufficient stabilization bounds without any time step restriction. The estimates dissipate the original convex energy and allow degenerate diffusion. We also extend the analysis to diffusion systems with a scalar energy potential in a fixed positive definite metric, and to consistent positive-weight quadrature discretizations. Applications include porous-medium flow, nonlinear heat transfer in plasma, and multicomponent diffusion.

papers.title: Dynamics-Aware Sampling and Recovery for Tensor-Valued Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: We study sampling and recovery for tensor-valued dynamical systems evolving under the t-product, using partial spatial observations over time. Although the t-product Fourier transform yields slicewise matrix dynamics, recovery does not generally decouple across slices. Eigenvalues shared across Fourier-domain frontal slices couple the corresponding eigenspaces into aggregated spectral blocks, which determine the tensor-specific recovery geometry and space--time tradeoff. We establish deterministic identifiability conditions for the initial tensor state. In the diagonalizable case, these are frame conditions on the aggregated blocks. We extend them to non-diagonalizable systems through generalized eigenspaces and Jordan structure. A temporal--spectral factorization of the finite-horizon stacked recovery system underlying Tensor Dynamical Sampling (DS) yields a decoupled two-stage formulation once the temporal threshold is reached. Under independent spatial subsampling, we prove high-probability recovery guarantees using empirical Gram matrices on the aggregated blocks. The bounds depend on aggregated multiplicities, incoherence, and population conditioning. Stability estimates separate the spatial frame factor from the temporal Vandermonde factor and show that increasing temporal depth may worsen numerical conditioning even after identifiability is ensured. We implement Tensor DS and evaluate it on synthetic and real data. Phase transitions track the predicted blockwise sampling thresholds, and stability experiments illustrate Vandermonde conditioning. Experiments on sea surface temperature and turbulence velocity data show that a learned t-product system operator generally yields more accurate and structurally faithful reconstructions than vectorized low-rank, Tucker-type, graph-regularized, graph-spectral, and vectorized dynamical sampling baselines.

papers.title: A Two-Grid Finite Element Method for the Nonlinear Poisson-Boltzmann Equation Based on a Solution Decomposition
papers.abstract: The nonlinear Poisson--Boltzmann equation (PBE) is a widely used implicit-solvent model for the electrostatics of biomolecules in ionic solvent. Its numerical solution is complicated by the point charges, the dielectric jump across the molecular surface, and the exponential nonlinearity. We study a two-grid finite element method for the PBE built on the solution decomposition $u=G+\Psi+\Phit$ of Xie [J.~Comput.~Phys.~275 (2014) 294--309], in which $G$ carries the singularities analytically, $\Psi$ solves a linear interface problem, and $\Phit$ solves a semilinear interface problem for an arbitrary number of ionic species. The nonlinear problem for $\Phit$ is solved on a coarse mesh only, followed by a single Newton correction on the fine mesh, so that only symmetric positive definite linear systems are solved on the fine mesh. The analysis uses a $C^2$ truncation of the exponential that grows quadratically beyond a level $\tau$; for $\tau$ above an explicit bound the truncated problem has the same solution as the original one, and no discrete maximum principle or mesh-angle condition is needed. Under standard piecewise regularity assumptions we prove quasi-optimal energy and $L^2$ estimates and an $L^4$ estimate for the finite element approximation of $\Phit$, and for the two-grid solution we prove $\enorm{u-\utg}\le C\big(h^{s-1}+H^{2(s-1)+t/2}\big)$ in three dimensions, where $t=\min\{s,\sigma\}-1$. Whenever the dual problem is at least as regular as the primal one ($\sigma\ge s$), the coarse mesh can be chosen as $H\sim h^{2/5}$ without loss of accuracy. A manufactured-solution test confirms the predicted rates and the quadratic dependence of the two-grid correction on the coarse error.

papers.title: A Discontinuous Galerkin Method for Biharmonic Dirichlet Control Problems With Patch Reconstruction
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present and analyze an interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin method for Dirichlet boundary control problems governed by the biharmonic equation, with the control imposed through the normal derivative. The method is based on a reconstructed discontinuous approximation that admits an arbitrarily high-order approximation space with only one unknown per element. We construct a discretization that approximates the state and adjoint state in this space and derive a priori error estimates in the energy and $L^2$ norms. The analysis is carried out under the limited regularity available on polygonal domains by means of a medius argument. Numerical experiments are provided to support the predicted convergence rates.

papers.title: An efficient coupled block preconditioner for the Marker-and-Cell discretization of the Stokes-Darcy equations
papers.abstract: We consider the iterative solution of the large, sparse and nonsymmetric double saddle-point systems arising from the stationary Stokes-Darcy equations in two dimensions, discretized by the Marker-and- Cell (MAC) finite difference method. Existing block triangular preconditioners rest on approximations of two Schur complements, the second of which is hard to approximate uniformly in the physical parameters. We propose instead a coupled preconditioner that keeps the interface coupling and regularizes the constraint block by a small multiple of the identity, so that the second Schur complement never has to be approximated. We analyze the spectrum of the preconditioned matrix, both in the ideal case and for the inexact version used in computations, and derive from it a rule for scaling the regularization parameter with the physical parameters. Numerical results show mesh-independent convergence of preconditioned GMRES and robustness with respect to the viscosity and the permeability.

papers.title: A High-Order Geometric-Compatible DGSEM with Subcell Limiting for the GPR System
papers.abstract: We construct an equation-of-state-independent geometric-compatible finite-volume (GC-FV) method and a high-order nodal discontinuous Galerkin spectral-element extension (GC-DG) for a reduced Godunov-Peshkov-Romenski system on fixed Eulerian meshes. Density is recovered from $\rho=\rho_0\det(\mathbf{A})$, so mass conservation is a hidden companion law of the distortion equation. Starting from a straight-path Dal Maso-LeFloch-Murat fluctuation pair, minimum-change cofactor projections produce a single-valued density flux and exact induced local Lax-Friedrichs dissipation without jump quotients. The summation-by-parts property lifts the geometric two-state identity to high order and yields an equivalent subcell representation of GC-DG. We then blend GC-DG with the compatible GC-FV operator on the same Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto subcells. Because both operators induce the same boundary density flux, the global subcell blend retains the exact semidiscrete mass balance while suppressing shock-generated oscillations. A complementary modal/face-jump indicator supplies the elementwise blending coefficient. Numerical experiments verify high-order convergence, the expected temporal scaling of the fully discrete mass drift, and robust shock capturing for fluid, nonlinear-elastic, thermal-wave, and elastoplastic problems, including genuinely multidimensional configurations.

papers.title: Active Flux and Polygons: why a stabilisation and how to implement boundary conditions
papers.abstract: In a recent paper, the authors developed an Active Flux-type algorithm for polygonal meshes (see \cite{BP_Pampa_VEM}). The main difference between Active Flux methods on polygonal meshes and those on Cartesian or simplex meshes is that the basis functions are not explicitly known. These functions describe the solution using point-value approximations on the polygon boundaries and the average value within the polygons. In \cite{BP_Pampa_VEM}, it was shown that directly transposing the algorithm from simplexes to polygons leads to a mild instability, and a remedy was proposed without a rigorous explanation. In the present paper, we clarify this issue and demonstrate that the solution presented in \cite{BP_Pampa_VEM} is indeed correct. Furthermore, another challenge-the implementation of boundary conditions-was previously solved heuristically. Building on \cite{pampa_dg}, we show how to properly implement these boundary conditions. Finally, the method is illustrated through several examples with hybrid meshes.

papers.title: Numerical Approximation of Maxwell Transmission Eigenvalue Problem in Dispersive Media via Holomorphic Operator Function
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop and analyze a numerical method for the Maxwell's transmission eigenvalue problem in dispersive media. The problem is formulated as the eigenvalue problem of a holomorphic Fredholm operator function of index zero. For discretization, we employ the Nedelec elements. Convergence of the scheme is established via the abstract approximation theory of Karma. To compute the resulting nonlinear matrix eigenvalue problems, we employ a parallel multi-step contour integral method. Numerical experiments are presented to demonstrate the viability and accuracy of the proposed approach.

papers.title: A discrete fractional Gr\"onwall inequality for dissipative systems via resolvent kernel estimate
papers.abstract: We establish a discrete fractional Gronwall inequality for dissipative systems with time-dependent forcing. For completely positive discretizations, we bound individual resolvent entries by integrals of the continuous response kernel, under controlled perturbation to the L1 weights and a stepsize restriction. The proof constructs a supersolution for each resolvent column. The resulting Mittag-Leffler weights retain both the decay of initial data and the historical contributions of forcing. The framework covers L1 and several standard schemes on uniform meshes. For linear subdiffusion, it yields decay-preserving L1 error estimates separating first order and $(2-\alpha)$ order contributions, with stronger long-time decay under additional solution regularity.
